summary: Implemented the durable provider-neutral ArtworkOperation write-ahead record, its phase and lifecycle-fence rules, and its generation-fenced authoritative store in src/ArrTags/Artwork, following ADR-003, docs/data-model.md sections 3.10.3 and 3.10.4, docs/architecture.md section 9, and Resolved Blocker 2. ArtworkOperationKind (Publication/Restoration) and ArtworkLifecycleFence (Normal/Disable/Uninstall/ItemRemoved) are the enum vocabulary. ArtworkOperationPhase matches the data-model table exactly (Prepared, MutationStarted, RepositoryUpdateStarted, VerificationPending, FinalizationPending, Committed, Aborted, RecoveryBlocked) and is documented as a durable lower-bound marker. ArtworkOperation carries modelVersion, operationId, kind, jellyfinItemId, imageSurface, generation, ownershipToken, priorPublicationToken, publicationToken, expectedBeforeIdentity, candidateAfterContentSha256, observedAfterIdentity, sourceArtifactId, derivedArtifactId, phase, lifecycleFence, attempt, lastError, createdAt, and updatedAt, plus explicit sourcePresence and candidateAfterPresence fields that make the documented conditional rules enforceable. Validate enforces every conditional requirement: a valid item/surface/operation id; a publication requires a present after target, a publication token, and a derived artifact; a restoration must target the same presence as its source baseline, must target the retained source content for a present source, and cannot carry a publication token or derived artifact; a present source requires a content-addressed source artifact; a present after target requires its SHA-256 content hash; generation and attempt are bounded; ownership/prior/publication tokens and artifact references are opaque and bounded; no path or credential field is present. ArtworkOperationErrors redacts control characters and bounds lastError to 512 characters. ArtworkOperationPhases is the pure phase-advance helper: CanAdvance/TryAdvance permit exactly one forward step along the documented order or a terminal outcome (Committed/Aborted/RecoveryBlocked) from any non-terminal phase, refuse backward and same-phase moves, and refuse to advance out of Committed, Aborted, or RecoveryBlocked; IsTerminal and the fail-safe MayHaveStartedMutation (only Prepared proves no mutation started) encode the lower-bound semantics. ArtworkOperationFencing provides the pure decisions AllowsNewPublication (Normal only), AllowsNewRestoration (except ItemRemoved), IsStale, CanSupersede, and IsSameGeneration, with no lifecycle event wiring. ArtworkOperationStore persists through the existing versioned, integrity-tagged, atomically-written StateRepository/StateAuthority.Authoritative boundary, keyed per item/image surface so only one operation can exist for a subject at a time; it validates on write, quarantines a valid-envelope-but-invalid payload rather than replaying it, fences writes by the monotonic generation (a stale generation cannot overwrite a newer durable record; a newer generation supersedes; the same generation may only advance the same operation through a legal phase), and marks only terminal phases (Committed, Aborted, or RecoveryBlocked) eligible for terminal-provenance retention so a non-terminal operation is never pruned (a tombstoned item-removal operation is terminal because its phase is Aborted, not because of its lifecycle fence). The store performs no image mutation and never calls SaveImage; task 5.5 drives the write-before-mutation ordering. docs/data-model.md section 3.10.3 now records the two explicit presence fields. New tests in ArtworkOperationTests, ArtworkOperationStoreTests, and the shared ArtworkOperationFixtures (101 cases) cover every conditional requirement, absent-versus-present after target, token bounds, lastError redaction, the phase enum and every legal/illegal transition, the fence decisions, durability across a reconstructed StateRepository, generation fencing, one-non-terminal-per-subject, authoritative quarantine on a corrupt or semantically invalid record, and terminal-versus-non-terminal retention. No ADR, RenderVersion, renderer behavior, MediaBrowser.* reference, lock file, or existing passing behavior was changed.

known_limitations: No Jellyfin image mutation, SaveImage call, item repository update, publication, reconciliation action, or lifecycle event wiring is implemented, by task scope. The store only persists and reads the durable record; task 5.5 drives the write-before-mutation ordering and task 5.7 owns recovery actions.

The store deliberately allows a strictly newer generation to supersede a non-terminal durable record (the documented 'a newer generation replaces/advances' rule). It cannot reconcile the superseded operation itself; the caller is responsible for resolving a non-terminal operation before accepting a new generation, and the per-subject record id still guarantees at most one persisted operation per item/surface.

ArtworkOperation gains explicit sourcePresence and candidateAfterPresence fields beyond the flat data-model 3.10.3 field list; this is required to make the task's conditional rules (a present source requires a source artifact, a present after target requires its content hash, an explicit absent after target) enforceable. docs/data-model.md section 3.10.3 was updated to record them; no ADR was changed.

lastError redaction strips control characters and bounds the summary to 512 characters but does not perform pattern-based secret detection, because no secret format is defined in the artwork namespace; the field remains a caller-supplied already-redacted diagnostic, matching the existing ArrProviderError boundary convention.

The model does not require a content hash on a present expectedBeforeIdentity or observedAfterIdentity, because a present-without-hash identity is a legal (if unusable) observation and ownership comparison fails closed on it; the operation record can represent that observation for recovery diagnostics.

No live-host, native-Skia, or package-content validation was performed for this task because it performs no image or host work; the environment-guarded Skia/host/package tests remain skipped under the default run exactly as before.
The new store and model are public and directly constructible but are not registered in ArrTagsServiceRegistrator; DI wiring belongs with the publication/reconciliation tasks that consume them.
